messages.subject: geom_point question
parts:
Given the following data frame and plot:
 
df <- data.frame(c(1,2,3,4,5), c(1,2,3,4,5), c(3,12,9,5,11))
names(df) <- c("x", "y", "z")
p <- ggplot()
p <- p + geom_point(data=df, aes(x=x, y=y, size=z))
 
What would be the best way to replot the data such that the point size ranges from 0 to 15 although these values are not in “z”?
 
Thanks in advance.

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: geom_point question
parts:
On 12/12/14 7:47 AM, Casault, Benoit wrote:
> Given the following data frame and plot:
>
> df <- data.frame(c(1,2,3,4,5), c(1,2,3,4,5), c(3,12,9,5,11))
> names(df) <- c("x", "y", "z")
> p <- ggplot()
> p <- p + geom_point(data=df, aes(x=x, y=y, size=z))
>
> What would be the best way to replot the data such that the point size
> ranges from 0 to 15 although these values are not in “z”?

I'm not exactly clear on what you want. Do you want the range of z
values (3-12) mapped onto point sizes 0-15? That would be

p + scale_size_continuous(range = c(0, 15))

Do you wan the scale that you saw in the original plot extended to
include the values 0 through 15? That would be

p + scale_size_continuous(limits=c(0,15))

Do you want the values listed in z to be the literal point sizes?

p + scale_size_identity()

Do you want the values listed in z to be the literal point sizes and a
guide given which goes from 0 to 15?

p + scale_size_identity(guide=guide_legend(), limits=c(0,15))

I would also suggest you consider

p + scale_size_area()
p + scale_size_area(limits=c(0,15))

If z represents a real quantity of something, this makes the areas
proportional to the amount, not the diameter, as that matches human
perception more accurately. See the help for scale_size_area for more
details.
